summary.text: Gwen Moore is the Democratic incumbent representing Wisconsin's 4th District (Milwaukee) since 2005, the first African American elected to Congress from Wisconsin. Before Congress she was a VISTA volunteer, a housing and social services official, and a state legislator for 15 years. She serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the Joint Economic Committee and is seeking another term.

paragraphs.text: Born in Racine, Wisconsin, in 1951 and raised in Milwaukee, the eighth of nine children; her father was a union factory worker and her mother a public school teacher. She attended North Division High School in Milwaukee, where she was student council president.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Marquette University, which she says she attended as a single, expectant mother with help from the federal TRIO program; she later earned a Harvard University Certificate for Senior Executives in State and Local Government in 2000. Sources differ on the year of her Marquette degree.
As a VISTA volunteer, helped start a community credit union and received the national "VISTA Volunteer of the Decade" award for 1976-1986, according to her official biography.

Worked as a housing officer for the Wisconsin Housing Development Authority; WUWM, drawing on her campaign website, says she worked for the City of Milwaukee and the state on housing and social services issues.
Served two terms in the Wisconsin State Assembly (1989-1992) and in the Wisconsin State Senate from 1993 to 2004.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2004, defeating Republican attorney Gerald Boyle with 69.6% of the vote according to Wikipedia, and became the first African American elected to Congress from Wisconsin; she took office on January 3, 2005.

Serves on the House Ways and Means Committee (Tax, Social Security, and Work and Welfare subcommittees) and the Joint Economic Committee, and co-chairs the bipartisan Congressional Caucus on Foster Youth. She previously served on the Financial Services, Science, Space, and Technology, and Budget committees.
Served as Democratic co-chair of the Congressional Women's Caucus from 2011 to 2013 and is a member of the Congressional Black Caucus and the Congressional Progressive Caucus, among others.
Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary over Amy Donahue, 70.5% to 29.3%. WUWM describes her as Wisconsin's longest-serving current member of the state's U.S. House delegation.
According to her official biography, she is the mother of three and a grandmother and great-grandmother.
